messages:
elena: Quick heads-up — ran an SNR robustness probe on the new cinder-embed-v2 quant candidates and seeing a weird recall@1 drop when we add noisy prefixes.
raj: ugh, how big a drop? can you paste the numbers? :thinking:
elena: baseline fp16 recall@1 = 0.782, int6-perchannel = 0.768 overall, but with 20% token-level gaussian noise on prefix recall@1 falls to 0.62 for int6 and 0.75 for fp16. recall@5 is less affected.
raj: that's substantial. so noise hurts int6 much more. did you run with KV-cache enabled?
elena: yes, same config as onboard tests: kv cache on, seq len 256, batch 64. Full command I used:```python
./eval_embed.py --model cinder-embed-v2 --quant int6_perchannel --batch 64 --kv_cache True --noise gaussian --noise_p 0.2 --metrics recall@1,5,10,silhouette,purity
```
raj: nice. can you dump config + sample noisy inputs? might be tokenization edge-case.
elena: uploaded a small sample to the run: s3://redwood-evals/cinder/snr_probe/samples.txt. Sample shows noise injected both in whitespace and token corruptions.
mike: tagging in server infra — @mike: any runtime differences observed (latency/soft-errors) between per-channel and per-tensor int6 builds?
mike: latency pretty comparable (+3% int6), no OOMs, but we did see a couple of soft-fallbacks to fp16 on node A (investigating).
tara: do we have cluster-level metrics for clustering quality? silhouette/purity numbers?
elena: silhouette(fp16)=0.41, silhouette(int6_perchannel)=0.39 baseline; with noise: fp16=0.36, int6=0.22. cluster purity @k5 baseline fp16=0.81, int6=0.79; with noise fp16=0.77, int6=0.60.
raj: ok that's consistent with recall drop. smells like quantization amplifies small perturbations in embedding space. could be reduced dynamic range or reduced angular resolution.
mike: quick thought — try per-channel with symmetric clipping vs asymmetric; and test small calibration set that includes noisy prefixes.
elena: doing that now. also trying hybrid-int6 where first 6 dims remain fp16 as a toy.
eval-bot: rundata:
- model: cinder-embed-v2
- candidates: fp16, int6_perchannel_sym, int6_pertensor, hybrid6
- dataset: anchor-holdout-10k + noisy-prefix-augment
- top-line: int6_perchannel_sym improved recall@1 (noisy) from 0.62 -> 0.67 but still below fp16 0.75

elena: quick log snippet from int6_perchannel_sym run:```
Recall@1: 0.672
Recall@5: 0.913
Silhouette: 0.28
Cluster purity@5: 0.68
```
tara: does the noisy-prefix augmentation distribution match production? if not we might be overfitting calibration.
elena: it's conservative — we injected noise at 5–25% token corruption and mixed whitespace/punctuation flips, which mimics user typos and copy/paste artifacts we've seen.
raj: next steps: 1) run int6_perchannel_sym with calibration set that includes noisy examples; 2) test per-tensor with larger calibration bins; 3) sanity-check tokenization differences vs fp16 by computing angular histogram of high-dim vectors for identical inputs.
mike: I'll check node A fallbacks and patch a kernel mismatch if needed.
eval-bot: new run queued: 4420135820 (int6_perchannel_sym + noisy-calib)
elena: thanks — will post updated numbers in this thread. if int6 can't match fp16 under realistic noise we should flag for rollback on the canary. :exclamation: 
raj: agreed. also add recall@1 broken down by query length buckets (short <10, medium 10–50, long >50). early hypothesis is short queries are more sensitive.
elena: added that to the run. preliminary: short queries recall@1 (int6 noisy) = 0.52 vs fp16=0.71. medium = 0.68 vs 0.76. long ~= parity.
tara: good diagnostic. short queries often have lower SNR so quantization hits harder. can we try tiny-temp scaling of embeddings (multiplicative rescale) before L2 norm? maybe that stabilizes angles.
raj: yeah try scaling factor sweep [0.95,1.0,1.05,1.1], see if small rescale reduces angular quantization error.
elena: queued scale sweep. thanks everyone, will update when runs finish. :thumbsup!
